senses.definition: not only so, but
examples: I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice

senses.definition: a body of students who graduate together
examples: the class of '97
she was in my year at Hoehandle High

senses.definition: a period of time containing 365 (or 366) days
examples: she is 4 years old
in the year 1920

senses.definition: a period of time occupying a regular part of a calendar year that is used for some particular activity
examples: a school year

senses.definition: the period of time that it takes for a planet (as, e.g., Earth or Mars) to make a complete revolution around the sun
examples: a Martian year takes 687 of our days

senses.definition: desire strongly or persistently
have a desire for something or someone who is not present
examples: She ached for a cigarette
I am pining for my lover

senses.definition: have affection for; feel tenderness for
a loud utterance of emotion (especially when inarticulate)
examples: a cry of rage
a yell of pain

senses.definition: a loud utterance; often in protest or opposition
examples: the speaker was interrupted by loud cries from the rear of the audience

senses.definition: utter a sudden loud cry
examples: she cried with pain when the doctor inserted the needle
I yelled to her from the window but she couldn't hear me

senses.definition: utter or declare in a very loud voice
examples: You don't have to yell — I can hear you just fine

senses.definition: affected by jaundice which causes yellowing of skin etc
changed to a yellowish color by age
examples: yellowed parchment

senses.definition: cowardly or treacherous
examples: the little yellow stain of treason
too yellow to stand and fight

senses.definition: easily frightened
of the color intermediate between green and orange in the color spectrum; of something resembling the color of an egg yolk
typical of tabloids
examples: sensational journalistic reportage of the scandal
yellow press

senses.definition: yellow color or pigment; the chromatic color resembling the hue of sunflowers or ripe lemons
turn yellow
examples: The pages of the book began to yellow

senses.definition: an affirmative
examples: I was hoping for a yes

senses.definition: in the recent past; only a short time ago
examples: I was not born yesterday!

senses.definition: on the day preceding today
examples: yesterday the weather was beautiful

senses.definition: the day immediately before today
examples: it was in yesterday's newspapers

senses.definition: the recent past
examples: yesterday's solutions are not good enough
we shared many yesterdays

senses.definition: despite anything to the contrary (usually preceding a concession)
examples: although I'm a little afraid, however I'd like to try it
while we disliked each other, nevertheless we agreed
he was a stern yet fair master
granted that it is dangerous, all the same I still want to go

senses.definition: to a greater degree or extent; used with comparisons
examples: looked sick and felt even worse
an even (or still) more interesting problem
still another problem must be solved
a yet sadder tale

senses.definition: up to the present time
examples: I have yet to see the results
details are yet to be worked out

senses.definition: used after a superlative
examples: this is the best so far
the largest drug bust yet

senses.definition: used in negative statement to describe a situation that has existed up to this point or up to the present time
examples: So far he hasn't called
the sun isn't up yet

senses.definition: within an indefinite time or at an unspecified future time
examples: he longed for the flowers that were yet to show themselves
sooner or later you will have to face the facts
in time they came to accept the harsh reality
